Disclosure  to  Promote  the  Right  To  Information 

Whereas  the  Parliament  of  India  has  set  out  to  provide  a  practical  regime  of  right  to 
information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public.

FOREWORD 

This  Indian  Standard  ( First  Revision  )  was  adopted  by  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards,  after  the 
draft  finalized  by  the  Meteorological  Instruments  Sectional  Committee  had  been  approved  by  the 
Light  Mechanical  Engineering  Division  Council. 

This  standard  was  originally  published  in  1968.  This  revision  is  based  on  the  further  experience 
gained  in  the  manufacture  of  meteorological  instruments  and  other  developments  in  this  field. 

Main  modifications  carried  out  in  this  revision  arc  as  under; 

a)  Good  quality  plastic  conforming  to  quality  requirements  laid  down  in  IS  10073  :  1982  has 
been  incorporated  in  material  clause 

b)  Separate  clause  for  referred  standards  in  this  specification   has  been    incorporated   as 
Clause  2  References. 

c)  Clauses  referring  to  construction  and  finish  and  marking  have  been  modified. 

d)  Requirements  for  rain  measures  used  in  recording  type  raingauges  have  been  incorporated. 

Accuracy  in  the  measurement  of  rainfall  is  of  great  importance  in  almost  all  fields  of  the  national 
economy  and  is  of  special  significance  in  agriculture,  irrigation,  flood  control,  power  generation 
and  the  conservation  of  water  resources  on  both  national  and  international  scales.  The  Director 
General  of  Meteorology,  New  Delhi  has  accordingly  been  designated  the  sole  authority  for 
ensuring  the  correct  rainfall  registration  in  India  and  is  responsible  for  the  testing  and  certification 
of  all  rain  gauges  and  rain  measures  used  in  the  country  by  rainfall  registration  authorities.  With 
the  increasing  manufacture  and  use  of  rain  measures  in  the  country  and  the  diflliculties  which  have 
arisen  in  their  test  and  certification,  it  has  become  necessary  to  prepare  this  standard. 

Rain  measures  are  used  with  rain  or  snow  gauges  for  the  measurement  of  precipitation  collected 
in  the  gauges.  The  existing  rain  measures  for  which  the  following  IMD  specifications  are  available, 
have  been  designed  for  use  with  rain  gauges  having  collector  diameters  of  127  and  203  mm: 

No,  34A  —  10  mm  measure  glass  for  127  mm  rain  gauge 
No.  35 A  ~  Measure  glass  for  127  mm  rain  gauge 
No.  36A  —  Measure  glass  for  203  mm  rain  gauge 

The  present  standard,  being  part  of  a  series  of  Indian  Standards  on  meteorological  instruments, 
deals  with  the  rain  measures  designed  for  use  with  the  new  standardized  rain  gauge  system. 

For  accurate  measurement  of  all  quantities  of  rain,  tapered  rain  measures  have  been  recommended 
by  the  World  Meteorological  Organization,  Geneva  and  are  used  in  some  countries.  Considering 
the  average  amount  of  rainfall  to  be  measured  in  India  and  the  convenience  in  manufacture  and 
use,  rain  measures  of  uniform  cross-section  have  been  prescribed  in  this  standard. 

This  standard  has  clause  8.1  which  provides  for  agreement  between  the  purchaser  and  the  supplier. 

For  the  purpose  of  deciding  whether  a  particular  requirement  of  this  standard  is  complied  with, 
the  final  value,  observed  or  calculated,  expressing  the  result  of  a  test  or  analysis,  shall  be  rounded 
off  in  accordance  with  IS  2  :  I960  *Rules  for  rounding  off  numerical  values  (  revised  )\  The  number 
of  significant  places  retained  in  the  rounded  off  value  should  be  the  same  as  that  of  the  specified 
value  in  this  standard. 


IS  4849  :  1992 


Indian  Standard 

METEOROLOGY  -  RAIN  MEASURES  - 

SPECIFICATION 

(  First  Revision  ) 


1  SCOPE 

1.1  This  standard  specifies  the  requirements  for 
ram  measures  for  use  with  ram  gauges  havmg 
collector  areas  of  200  cm^ 

2  REFERENCES 

2.1  The  following  Indian  Standards  are  necessary 
adjuncts  to  this  standard. 

JS  No  Title 

1382:  1981  Glossary  of  terms  relating  to 
glass  and  glassware  (  first 
revision  ) 

2'^03  1963  Method  of  grading  glass  for 
alkalinity 

4426  1967  Methods  of  sampling  laboratory 
glassware  and  medical  glass 
instruments 


10073  .  1982 

3  TERMINOLOGY 


Plastics     giadualcd     measuring 
cylinders 


3.1  For  the  purpose  ot  this  standard,   the  defini- 
tions gnen  in  IS  1382     1981  shall  apply 

4  DESIGNATION 

4.1  In  this  specification   the  si/e   designation   ol 

lam   measures   is   expressed  by     its     type,     for 

example,   Type    I,    Type   2,  Type  3,  Type  4  and 
Type  5 

5  TYPES 

5.1  The  ram  measures  shall   be  of  the  following 
types 

a)  Type  1  -  20  mm  capacity  ram  measure 
suitable  for  use  with  precipitation  gauges 
having  collectors  of  200  cm^  area, 

b)  Type  2  —  10  mm  capacity  rain  measure 
suitable  for  use  with  piecipilation  gauges 
having  collectors  of  200  cm-^  area, 

c)  Type  3  —  20  mm  capacity  rain  measure 
suitable  for  use  with  precipitation  gauges 
having  collectors  of  100  cm^  area; 

d)  Type  4—10  mm  capacity  ram  measure 
for  325  cm*  recording  rain  gauge,  and 


e)  Type  5       25  mm  capacity  rain    measure 
for  130  cm*  recording  rain  gauge 

NOTLS 

1  Types  2  cind  3  have  jdcntical  dimensions  but  arc 
graduated  ditRrenlly  for  Use  wilh  200  cni^  and  100  cm' 
tollcctors  respectively 

2  Tvpes  4  and  ^  have  id  ntical  dimensions  but  arc 
graduated  diiFcienlly  for  use  with  325  and  130  cm^ 
collectors  used  in  recording  lain  gauges 

6  REQUIREMENTS 

6.1  Material 

The  ram  measure  shall  be  made  of  colourless  and 
transparent  glass  They  shall  be  as  free  as  possi- 
ble trom  stones,  air  bubbles,  striae,  cords  and 
other  visible  defects  The  graduated  portion, 
however,  shall  be  free  from  all  such  defects 
They  shall  also  be  well-annealed  and  as  far  as 
possible,  of  uniform  thickness  throughout,  of 
approximately  2  mm  Good  quality  plastic  con- 
forming to  quality  requirements  laid  down  m 
IS  10073     1982  can  also  be  considered 

6.1.1  Limit  of  Alkalinity 

The  glass  of  rain  measures  when  tested  according 
to  the  method  prescribed  in  IS  2303  1963  shall 
conform  to  Type  2 

6.2  Construction  and  I'lnish 

The  rain  measures  shall  be  cylindrical  flat  bottom- 
ed containers  having,  as  far  as  possible,  a  uniform 
diameter  The  open  end  shall  be  splayed  and 
provided  with  a  lip,  the  edges  being  well  rounded 
off  The  base  shall  be  either  circulai  or  of  any 
other  form  provided  the  rain  measures  satisfy  the 
requirements  prescribed  m  6.2.1  They  shall  be 
so  constructed  that  when  placed  on  a  horizontal 
plane  surface  they  shall  stand  vertically  without 
rocking  or  spinning. 

6.2.1  The  rain  measures  shall  not  topple  when 
placed  empty  on  a  surface  inclined  at  an  angle 
of  10"  to  the  horizontal 

6.3  Dimensions 

The  dimensions  of  the  rain  measures  shall  be  as 
given  m  Fig    1,  2,  3,  4  and  5 


I 


IS  4849  :  1992 


6.4  Graduation  and  Figuring 

6.4.1  The  graduation  marks  shall  be  horizontal 
lines.  They  shall  be  fine,  clear  permanent  lines 
of  uniform  thickness,  lying  in  planes  perpendicular 
to  the  axes  of  the  rain  measure^.  There  shall  be 
no  evident  irregularity  in  the  spacing  of  the 
graduation  marks.  A  very  slight  non-uniformity 
in  the  lowest  few  graduations  is  permissible,  if 
unavoidable,  provided  they  are  accurately 
calibrated. 

6.4.1.1  The  graduations  shall  be  marked  for 
every  0' I  or  0*2  mm  as  shown  in  Fig.  1,2,3,4 
and  5. 

6.4.1.2  The  centres  of  the  graduation  marks  shall 
lie  in  a  vertical  line  down  the  front  of  the  rain 
measure  when  it  is  standing  on  a  horizontal  sur- 
face with  the  spout  on  the  left. 

6.4.2  Every  full  mm  graduation  line  shall  be 
plainly  figured',  round  by  figures  not  less  than  4 
or  5  mm  high,  to  the  right  of  and  immediately 
opposite  to  the  end  of  the  graduation  line  as 
shown  in  Fig.  I,  2,  .3,  4  and  5.  They  shall  be 
placed  in  such  a  way  that  they  are  bisected  by  an 
extension  of  the  line  to  which  they  refer.  Alter- 
nately, the  figures  shall  be  placed  immediately 
above  the  extended  line  to  which  they  refer. 

6.4.2.1  The  position  of  the  unit  digit  of  all  figures 
shall  be  roughly  between  two  lines  parallel  to  the 
axes  of  the  rain  measures. 

6.4.2.2  All  graduations  and  figures  shall  be  of 
uniform  thickness  and  shall  be  finely  marked  with 
permanent  colour. 

6.5  Basis  of  Calibration 

The  rain  measures  of  Type  1  corresponding  to 
20  mm  of  rainfall  shall  contain  40000  cm» 
or  39842  g  of  distilled  water  when  filled  to  their 
highest  graduation  mark  at  2TC,  65  percent  rela- 
tive humidity  and  760  mm  of  mercury  pressure. 
The  capacity  corresponding  to  10  mm  and  20  mm 
of  rainfall  in  Types  2  and  3  shall  be  20000  cm^ 
of  199*21  g  of  distilled  water  when  filled  to  the 
highest  graduation  mark  at  27X.  Types  4  and  5 
measure  glasses  shall  contain  325  cm'  or  32372  g 
of  distilled  water  corrcspondmg  to  10  m  and 
25  mm  of  rainfall  respectively  when  filled  to  the 
highest  graduation  mark  at  27*'C,  65  percent 
relative  humidity  and  760  mm  of  mercury 
pressure,  against  brass  weights.  The  lower  edge 
of  the  water  meniscus  being  in  the  horizontal 
plane  containing  the  graduation  mark. 


6.6  Tolerances 

The  maximum  permissible  error  at  any  point  as 
also  the  maximum  permissible  difTeiencc  between 
errors  at  any  two  points  not  less  than  10  sub- 
divisions removed  from  one  another,  shall  be 
±0*05  mm  of  rainfall  in  the  measure  glass  having 
capacity  of  10  mm  rainfall,  while  it  shall  be 
iO'l  mm  for  the  measure  glass  having  capacity  of 
20  and  25  mm  rainfall.  For  testing  and  when  using 
the  measure,  the  scale  reading  shall  correspond  to 
the  position  of  the  lower  edge  of  the  water 
meniscus. 


7  MARKING 

7.1  The  rain  measures   shall 
mscriptions  marked  legibly: 

a) 


bear  the   following 


The  marks  *10  mm  rainfall'  or  *20  mm 
rainfair  or  *25  mm  rainfalF,  as  the  case 
may  be  above  the  scale  between  the  highest 
graduation  marks  and  the  top  of  the  rain 
measure; 

b)  The  inscriptions  *Rain  Measure  for  130  cm^ 
200  cm^  325  cni'^  Collector'  or  *Rain 
Measure  for  100  cm^  Collector',  as  the  case 
may  be,  marked  either  to  the  left  of  the 
scale  or  on  the  side  opposite  to  (  a  )  above, 
at  the  top  of  the  rain  measure.  In  case  of 
recording  rain  gauge,  the  inscription 
*  Measure  glass  for  10  mm  recording  rain 
gauge'  or  'Measure  glass  for  25  mm  recor- 
dmg  rain  gauge'  as  the  case  may  be,  engra- 
ved to  the  left  of  the  scale; 

c)  The  marker's  name  or  his  recognized  trade- 
mark; and 

d)  The  serial  number  and  year  of  manufacture, 
for  example,  'No.   1234/92'. 


7.1.1  Standard  Mark 

Details  available   with    the 
Standards. 


Bureau    of    Indian 


8  PACKING 

8.1  The  rain  measures  shall  be  packed  in  card- 
board cartons  suitably  cushioned,  as  agreed  to 
between  the  purchaser  and  the  supplier. 

9  TESTING  AND  INSPECIION 

9.1  Each  Rain  Measure  shall  be  tested  individu- 
ally for  conformity  to  all  the  requirements  of  this 
specification.

Standard  Mark 

The  use  of  the  Standard  Mark  is  governed  by  the  pTovmoM  of  iht  Bureau  of  Indian 
Standards  Act,  1986  and  the  Rules  and  Regulations  made  thereunder.  The  Standard  Mark  on 
products  covered  by  an  Indian  Standard  conveys  the  assurance  that  they  have  been  produced 
to  comply  with  the  requirements  of  that  standard  under  a  well  defined  system  of  inspection, 
testing  and  quality  control  which  is  devised  and  supervised  by  BIS  and  operated  by  the 
producer.  Standard  marked  products  arc  also  continuously  checked  by  BIS  for  conformity 
to  that  standard  as  a  further  safeguard.  Details  of  conditions  under  which  a  licence  for  the 
use  of  the  Standard  Mark  may  be  granted  to  manufacturers  or  producers  may  be  obtained 
from  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards. 


Bureau  of  Indian  Standards 

BIS  is  a  statutory  institution  established  under  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  Acu  1986  to  promote 
harmonious  development  of  the  activities  of  standardization,  marking  and  quality  certification  of  goods 
and  attending  to  connected  matters  in  the  country. 

Copyright 

BIS  has  the  copyright  of  all  its  publications.  No  part  of  these  publications  may  be  reproduced  in 
any  form  without  the  prior  permission  in  writing  of  BIS,  This  does  not  preclude  the  free  use,  in  the 
course  of  implementing  the  standard,  of  necessary  details,  such  as  symbols  and  sizes,  type  or  grade 
designations.     Enquiries  relating  to  copyright  be  addressed  to  the  Director  (  Publications  ).  BIS. 

ReTislon  of  Indian  Standards 

Indian  Standards  are  reviewed  periodically  and  revised,  when  necessary  and  amendments,  if  any,  are 
issued  from  time  to  time.  Users  of  Indian  Standards  should  ascertain  that  they  are  in  possession  of 
the  latest  amendments  or  edition.  Comments  on  this  Indian  Standard  may  be  sent  to  BiS  giving  the 
following  reference :
